# ALGAL

{{SITE_DESCRIPTION}}

Agent programs today are scripts: they run start to finish and leave a log. ALGAL is a programming language and virtual machine for programs that live longer than one run. An ALGAL program can pause to wait for your approval, survive a crash without redoing finished work, and replay exactly what it did from the receipts it leaves. The VM is previewing now, and the language toolchain ships with it. ALGAL is free and open source.

ALGAL is prerelease software. Unsigned native builds for macOS on Apple silicon and Linux x86_64 are published as GitHub prereleases.

## Pages

- [Write agent programs that wait, resume, and replay](https://algal.computer/): what an ALGAL program can do, the source language, the habitat it runs in, receipts, and how programs propose new programs
- [Inside a living program](https://algal.computer/tour/): the guided tour, with recorded runs, interactive diagrams you can replay, source diagnostics, and composition examples
- [Put living programs to work](https://algal.computer/use-cases/): change review, checked coding repairs, portable run histories, reusable routing, and current limits
- [Documentation index](https://algal.computer/docs/): the repository docs rendered for the web, covering install, the source language, the process VM, habitats, civilization, and executors
- [Notes on living programs](https://algal.computer/blog/): longer posts on how the language works, how it is tested, and the design choices behind it
- [Comparisons](https://algal.computer/compare/): how ALGAL compares with LangGraph, DSPy, and Temporal

{{BLOG_POSTS}}

## Comparisons

- [ALGAL vs LangGraph](https://algal.computer/compare/langgraph/): agent orchestration framework versus a language and VM where the program is data
- [ALGAL vs DSPy](https://algal.computer/compare/dspy/): prompt-space optimization inside a fixed pipeline versus measured search over program structure
- [ALGAL vs Temporal](https://algal.computer/compare/temporal/): durable execution service versus portable, verifiable program artifacts

## Limits

- Site examples use scripted model answers. Every run published on the site has a receipt that was replay-checked when the site was built.
- A receipt that verifies shows the run was internally consistent. It does not show that a model's answer is true or that a provider performed an operation.
- Programs can propose new programs as data. The host decides which ones are checked, measured, and kept.
